title: The Same Chart, Twice the Pixels: Logical and Device Coordinates

questions.question: An image is created 200 by 120 for a 100 by 60 chart on a screen with a device pixel ratio of 2, and the ratio is never set on the image. What gets drawn?
options: A quarter-size chart in the top left corner, with three quarters of the image empty
The chart, correctly, since the image is the right size
A chart stretched to fill the image
Nothing, since the coordinates are out of range
questions.explanation: Measured: 397 pixels of ink in a box 0,0..100,60 instead of 797 filling 0,0..199,119. The painter treats its coordinates as device pixels unless the image says otherwise.

questions.question: Why does this bug reach users rather than being caught in review?
options: At a ratio of 1 the correct and incorrect versions are pixel for pixel identical
The compiler cannot warn about it
It only happens on Windows
Qt changed the default between versions
questions.explanation: The person who writes it has a ratio of 1 and so does the test machine. The fault appears only on the screens somebody paid more for. Rendering the same drawing at 1 and at 2 and comparing bounding boxes is four lines of test.

questions.question: On a surface at ratio 2, how many device rows does a line inked with setWidth(0), setWidth(1) and setWidth(2) occupy?
options: 1, 2 and 4: a pen of width zero is cosmetic and means the thinnest line the device can draw
0, 1 and 2: width zero draws nothing
1, 1 and 2: widths are in device pixels
2, 2 and 4: everything is doubled
questions.explanation: setWidth(1) means one logical unit. A grid tuned to be unobtrusive at a ratio of 1 is twice as heavy at 2, while the text beside it stays the same weight.

questions.question: A line is drawn at logical x = 75 on a surface at ratio 2, and found in the rendered image at column 150. What is wrong with using 150 as the chart position?
options: It is off the end of a chart 100 units wide, and anything looking up the sample there clamps or indexes past the array
Nothing, 150 is the device position and that is what a hit test wants
It is only wrong by rounding
It should be 300, since the ratio applies twice
questions.explanation: The error is exactly the ratio, which is exactly zero on a machine where the ratio is 1. Convert at the boundary in one function, and keep everything above it logical.

questions.question: A colleague fixes the quarter-size chart by multiplying every coordinate by the ratio before painting. What breaks?
options: Every hit test, layout calculation and stored geometry, because now half the program is in one unit and half in the other
Nothing, it is an equivalent fix
Only the pen widths
The image size, which is now doubled twice
questions.explanation: Setting the ratio is what lets everything above that line stay in the units the layout is in. That is the point of having a ratio at all.

questions.question: Which lines should use a cosmetic pen and which a real logical width?
options: Hairlines for rules and gridlines, whose job is to be visible and not noticed; a logical width for anything that should look the same size on every screen
Cosmetic for everything, since it is always one pixel
Logical for everything, since it scales
It makes no difference at ratios above 1
questions.explanation: setWidth(1) is what you get by not choosing: too thin to be a deliberate thickness and too thick to be a hairline. A cosmetic pen also ignores the painter's transform, which is what a grid wants and never what a drawn object wants.
